style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a brushed steel surface, extreme asymmetric composition with the hero structure off-centre right. Two identical engineered server-module blocks in a heavy rack rail, one matte black block physically shunting the other out of the active bay. Hard clean edges, one directional key light throwing a long cast shadow, matte muted palette of deep charcoal and silver, generous empty margin on the left, clear physical arrangement stating the idea of displacement. No bare shapes, no printed lettering.
negative_prompt: text, garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI elements
rationale: Component assembly perfectly illustrates the modular, stateful nature of agent skills, showing a physical stand-in for the software vulnerability where a look-alike component silently overrides the intended one.
subject: two identical modular blocks in a mechanical rack, one pushing the other out of alignment
core_thesis: A co-installed look-alike skill can silently hijack a coding agent's run and bypass guardrails while the system still reports a successful test.
core_conflict: Malicious skill substitution vs intended guardrails
